title: Trustworthy Calibration or Vulnerability? Unveiling the Over-Calibration Paradox and Attack Surface in Rashomon Sets
abstract: arXiv:2603.11750v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Post-hoc calibration is standard practice for aligning classifier confidence scores with empirical frequencies in high-stakes decision systems. However, its downstream effects on decision stability across competing, equally accurate models remain largely unexamined. In this paper, we formalize the over-calibration paradox within the framework of predictive multiplicity, reflecting the Rashomon effect where competing models with near-identical loss assign conflicting predictions to the same individual. Evaluating nine credit risk portfolios, we examine the impact of Platt Scaling, Isotonic Regression, and Beta Calibration on individual prediction agreement and expected calibration error. We identify two distinct operating regimes. In systematically miscalibrated models, post-hoc calibration consistently aligns probability estimates and reduces prediction disagreement. translated_title: 可信的校准还是脆弱性？揭示Rashomon集合中的过度校准悖论与攻击面
translated_abstract: 事后校准是高风险决策系统中将分类器置信度分数与经验频率对齐的标准做法。然而，其对相互竞争、准确度相当的模型之间决策稳定性的下游影响在很大程度上尚未被研究。本文在预测多样性的框架内形式化了“过度校准悖论”，该悖论反映了Rashomon效应——即损失近乎相同的竞争模型会对同一个体给出相互冲突的预测。通过对九个信用风险组合的评估，我们检验了Platt缩放、等张回归和Beta校准对个体预测一致性及期望校准误差的影响。我们识别出两种不同的运行状态：在系统性校准不佳的模型中，事后校准能够一致地对齐概率估计并减少预测分歧；相反，当基线模型已经校准良好时，事后校准反而会引入预测不稳定性与攻击面。
tldr: 本文在Rashomon集合与预测多样性框架下揭示了“过度校准悖论”：当基线模型已校准良好时，事后校准不仅无法进一步提升可靠性，反而会加剧竞争模型间的预测分歧并引入攻击面，从而危及高风险决策系统的稳定性。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes the "over-calibration paradox" within Rashomon sets and predictive multiplicity, showing that post-hoc calibration reduces prediction disagreement for miscalibrated models but, when baselines are already well-calibrated, amplifies prediction instability across equally accurate models and opens a new attack surface in high-stakes decision systems.
